variables.notes: A bad value stops the script with exit status 1 (checks at lines 233-243). Option: -t or --max-tokens. The matching command-line option overrides the environment value.

variables.name: MAX_TOKENS_JITTER
variables.values: A non-negative integer of at most 9 digits with no leading zero. It must be smaller than MAX_TOKENS_BASE.
variables.default: Unset or empty: 128 tokens
variables.effect: It is the half-width of the random max_tokens range, so that requests do not all finish at the same time.

variables.values: An integer, at least 1 and not larger than PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX. The unit is estimated tokens (the script counts 3 words as 4 tokens).
variables.default: Unset or empty: 1000
variables.effect: It is the smallest prompt size in long mode. Each request draws its size at random between the minimum and the maximum.
variables.notes: A range that breaks the rule stops the script with exit status 1 (line 229). Not used for the prompt text in short mode. Option: -p or --prompt-min. The matching command-line option overrides the environment value.

variables.name: PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX
variables.values: An integer, not smaller than PROMPT_TOKENS_MIN. The unit is estimated tokens.
variables.default: Unset or empty: 15000
variables.effect: It is the largest prompt size in long mode.
variables.notes: The script header says that the served model needs a context window of at least PROMPT_TOKENS_MAX + MAX_TOKENS_BASE + MAX_TOKENS_JITTER. Option: -P or --prompt-max. The matching command-line option overrides the environment value.

variables.name: STREAMING
variables.values: Exactly the text true selects the streaming path of the script. The text false selects the blocking path. Usage texts and comments were read for names that the code does not expand. Two GNU make built-ins were added (MAKE, MAKEOVERRIDES), because the makefiles use them without assigning them and a measurement showed that the environment can supply both. The first inventory had left them out with the words 'the environment does not supply in normal use'. Measurements made outside the checkout (no repository script was run): GNU Make 4.3 with scratch makefiles for '?=' with an empty value, ifndef, ifdef, $(origin), MAKECMDGOALS, MAKELEVEL, MAKE, MAKEOVERRIDES, MAKEFLAGS, CURDIR and SHELL; nproc and mktemp of GNU coreutils 8.32 for OMP_THREAD_LIMIT, OMP_NUM_THREADS and TMPDIR; dash for the integer test of COVERAGE_BASELINE; jq for the STREAMING value. Three entries of rust/rust-toolchain.sh, REMOVE_GLOBAL, USER_INSTALL and VERBOSE, are shell variables that the script tests without first giving them a value. REMOVE_GLOBAL can lead to 'apt-get remove' of Rust packages when the script runs as root, and CMake runs the script at configure time (CMakeLists.txt:413-418).
